1: This kind of image easily gives people an idea: if only there were a model in a chat that could first figure out what the other person is saying, and then remind us what to do next—that seems pretty useful.
2: Before every answer, you go through a decision-making process.
3: This chapter starts with the simplest possible call: we hand a work message, a question, and a few options to an open-source decision model, and see how the model scores the options and how the program retrieves the corresponding answer. Once the call process is clear, you can swap in your own question and context.
4: Why has Jev sparked so much discussion?
5: On September 15, 2026, TypeSafe AI released Jev, calling it a System One Model. Officially, it targets fast, structured judgments within software. The name borrows the "fast thinking" analogy, and for now it can be understood as a kind of task positioning.
6: Suppose we're building an office assistant that already has tools for statistics, drafting copy, and so on. After receiving a new message, it must first pick the right tool before it can complete the task. If all it needs to do is decide which workflow to follow, what the program needs most is a clear option.
7: Of course, an ordinary large model can do this too. We can have it return a short answer, or output in a specified JSON structure. Jev instead turns this kind of judgment into a dedicated interface: input the background, question, and candidate options, and it returns results the program can use directly, along with corresponding probabilities.
8: This also explains why people building Agents care about it. Within a task, besides writing content, you may repeatedly encounter steps like choosing tools, filtering materials, and judging whether human handling is needed. Asking these questions clearly and then handing the results to code makes the whole process easier to check.
9: As for how much faster and cheaper it is, that has to be compared within specific tasks. Which model you use as a reference, how many questions you ask at once, and whether network latency is included all affect the results. The performance numbers on the release page are the vendor's own demos and test conditions, and cannot be taken directly as the results after we integrate it into our business.

37: The grading criteria in Score need to be defined in advance. For example, how to distinguish between an explicit statement that delivery is due today and no mention of timing at all must be told to it by us. The score obtained here expresses a judgment made according to this set of criteria and cannot be used directly to infer how anxious the other party really is.
38: Can so-called "zero hallucination" really guarantee a correct choice every time?
39: After seeing the input and output, you may ask: since it can only choose from the existing options, does that mean it won't make mistakes?
40: First separate the two cases. When letting the model write an answer, it may add information not present in the materials; after limiting the candidate options, the program can constrain the range of answers. For example, if only data summarization, copywriting, and insufficient information are allowed, an unfamiliar task name will not appear.
41: But it may still choose wrongly. It is clearly asking for a sales report, yet it is classified as copywriting; the resulting format is completely valid, but the subsequent work will still go in the wrong direction.
42: The zero in the "zero hallucination" diagram comes from the guarantee of a predetermined output structure and cannot be understood as a zero error rate for factual and semantic judgments.
43: For example, a merchant only sells standing desks, chairs, and monitor stands, but a user asks about a broken desk lamp. If the model is only allowed to choose among these three kinds of products, the desk lamp will also be assigned to the closest option, even if that option does not apply at all.
44: Therefore, when posing questions to the model, a way to handle "none of these options are suitable" must be left. In a business system, supplementary information, follow-up questions, or manual verification can also be arranged.
45: Probability must be viewed the same way. A candidate option having the highest score means the model prefers it among the current options and cannot be used to conclude that it has an equally high accuracy rate in the business context. The official documentation also distinguishes candidate probability from confidence; the latter reflects the concentration of the distribution, and the two should not be mixed up.
47: If you have worked on intent recognition, you will probably find this familiar. When a user says "book me a flight to Shanghai tomorrow," first determine that it is about booking a flight, then extract information such as "tomorrow" and "Shanghai," and then enter the booking process. As early as 2019, there was already work using BERT to jointly perform intent classification and slot filling.
48: This analogy makes sense; both are converting natural language into results that a program can use. However, for a specific call, you still need to be clear about what you want to get.

56: Decision-making under a limited set of candidates
57: Another easily confused point is when the options are determined. Common traditional classifiers fix their labels at training time; interfaces like Jev allow us to provide the question, options, and textual explanation at call time. When switching tasks, you can try a different set of descriptions.
58: But whether new options can be understood still depends on model capability and actual testing.
59: As for how the original Jev is specifically implemented internally, it is unknown. The full architecture and training data have not been made public, and the community's choice of BERT or Qwen to implement similar functionality cannot be used to infer the original structure.

121: First adjust the scores using the release temperature, then apply softmax. The result is a probability distribution over the candidates provided in this run, and all candidate probabilities sum to approximately 1. It is not an exhaustive enumeration of all possible answers, nor does it mean the option has an equally high accuracy rate in real business use.
122: The model first selects the item with the highest probability. best_index is the position, letters[best_index] is the candidate letter, and option_items[best_index] is the corresponding business key and description.
